## 1

In this activity, we will work with the `Prestige` data in the `carData` package.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data("Prestige", package = "carData")
```
:::



Look at the help page to better understand these data. Here, we want to predict the `income` of occupational incumbents from the average `education` of occupational incumbents. Use `ggplot` to create a scatterplot with one or more best-fit curves. What type of relationship do you think best characterizes the relationship between these variables?


::: {.cell}

:::


## 2

Fit a simple linear regression model predicting `income` from `education` and evaluate assumptions. What do you conclude?


::: {.cell}

:::


## 3

Looking ahead: the `lm` function takes formula input like we used with `geom_smooth()`. Fit a regression equation for the best-fit quadratic/cubic curve predicting `income` from `education`. You can find the model residuals in the same way as we did for the linear model. Do the quadratic or cubic models do a better job meeting our assumptions about residuals? If not, can you think of what might be a better solution?


::: {.cell}

:::
